summary: This bill prohibits federal funds, including Medicare and Medicaid, from being given to healthcare facilities that deny treatment to individuals based on their COVID-19 vaccination status.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly impacts healthcare by prohibiting federal funds to facilities that deny treatment based on COVID-19 vaccination status. This aims to ensure access to healthcare services regardless of vaccination status, which leans towards a more public-oriented approach to healthcare access by preventing discrimination.

The bill references titles XVIII, XIX, and XXI of the Social Security Act, which are Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP, respectively. By conditioning federal funds for facilities receiving these funds, it indirectly affects the administration and accessibility of these social safety net programs, ensuring that beneficiaries are not denied treatment based on vaccination status.

The bill conditions all federal health program funds (including Medicare/Medicaid) on providers not refusing treatment based on COVID-19 vaccination status. This is a direct government mandate expanding access to care and is the sole purpose of the legislation.
